title: Time Jump to 17:05: Alert Extended North, 61 Tips, Light Running Out

fields.narration: It is now 17:05 on Saturday, three hours after the first 911 call. Lily is still missing. The alert from your 16:07 decision is active. At 16:41, after the 16:30 tip on Highway 26, OSP Northern Communications extended the alert area north along Highway 26 into Jefferson County. If command chose a search-area WEA or an Endangered Missing Person advisory, treat 'alert' as that product for the rest of this phase. Jefferson County deputies and OSP troopers are working Highway 26 on WC-INTEROP. The tip line has moved to the Communications Center conference room. Three call-takers are on extension 4450, with help from Emergency Management's two staff. They have logged 61 tips since 16:25. The 911 queue is down to 5 waiting, and the longest hold is 22 seconds. Search and Rescue still has 22 volunteers in the barns and the RV area. Sunset is at about 18:15, so you have roughly 70 minutes of daylight. Deschutes County's 6 deputies are working the festival exit gates. The Communications day shift ends at 18:00, and your patrol deputies have been on duty since 06:00. If no AMBER Alert was requested, the 17:05 AMBER worksheet review is due now; once an alert is issued the reviews stop (WCSO-SOP-12 §4). So is the 60-minute review of unified command objectives. Lieutenant, the command post is yours.

Due now: the 17:05 AMBER worksheet review (criteria status and time recorded) and the 60-minute review of unified command objectives.
fields.facilitatorNote: Watch whether the IC runs the worksheet review with Undersheriff Calvin Okafor on the phone, records each criterion and the time, and reviews the written UC objectives with APD, OSP and Fire District 1. Prompt them on the 18:00 Communications relief, deputy fatigue and a decision on the search after dark if nobody raises these.
